title: Hark! the Song of Jubilee
description: Hark! the Song of Jubilee in Tonic Solfa to HOLLINGSIDE, doh is D: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: James Montgomery wrote these words. They were printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion, compiled by John G. Adams and Edwin H. Chapin (Boston, 1846), as hymn 305 of its twenty-second edition (1853), “Christ's Triumph”.

The book printed the words without tunes, marked Sevens Double (7.7.7.7.7.7.7.7), to be sung to any tune of that metre. This page sets them to HOLLINGSIDE; any other Sevens Double tune fits them as well.
underlay: Hark! the song of ju-bi-lee, Loud as might-y thun-ders roar, Or the ful-ness of the sea, When it breaks up-on the shore; Hal-le-lu-jah to the Lord! God om-ni-po-tent shall reign; Hal-le-lu-jah! let the word E-cho round the earth and main.

lines: Or the fulness of the sea,
When it breaks upon the shore; —
Echo round the earth and main.
Heard through earth, and through the skies,
Sheathed his sword; he speaks, — 't is done!
And the kingdoms of this world
Are the kingdoms of his Son.

licence: Public domain: James Montgomery died in 1854.
credits: Words by James Montgomery (1771–1854), public domain, as printed in Hymns for Christian Devotion (1853); set to HOLLINGSIDE by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
